 Judgment

This appeal is by the claimant aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award dated 29.01.2019 passed in ECA No.289/2014 on the file I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner for Employees Compensation at Vijayapura, in which, the Commissioner while partly NC:
2023:KHC-K:8642 allowing the claim petition filed by the appellant-claimant has awarded the compensation of Rs.5,68,425/- along with interest at 12% per annum from the date of incident.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the son of the claimant namely Laxmikant, who was working under the employment of respondent No.1 as Driver in his Tractor bearing registration No.
KA-33/TA-1233 and Trailer bearing No.KA-32/T-4619, on 05.04.2012 while proceeding in the said Tractor towards Hadanur Village to unload stones, near the land of one Parutayya, one buffalo suddenly crossed the road, due to which, he applied break and in the process he lost control of the vehicle and the same turned turtle and he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same on Smt. Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16179811/
2 the spot.

entities.text: Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A case was registered in Crime No.44/2012.

Thereupon a claim petition is filed under Section 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 seeking compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- by the claimant who is the mother of the claimant on the premise that the deceased was earning NC:
2023:KHC-K:8642 Rs.6,000/- p.m. and was contributing the entire amount for the family.
3.

In response to the notice, respondent No.1 appeared and filed statement of objections admitting the fact that the deceased was working as a tractor and trailer driver under him and that he was holding valid driving license and was paid Rs.5,000/- as a salary.

It is contended that the vehicle was fully insured at the time of the accident and liability if any would be of the respondent No.2.
Hence, sought for rejection of the claim petition.
4. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company in the statement of objection had denied the claim averments and also denied the relationship between the deceased and the respondent No.1 and also denied that deceased was holding valid driving license.
It is also contended that vehicle did not have permit to ply and accident had taken place outside the permitted area.

That there was a breach of policy conditions, as such sought for dismissal of the petition.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 5.
The Commissioner framed the issues and recorded the evidence.

On appreciation of the evidence,
the Commissioner, came to the conclusion that there was a relationship of employer and the employee between the respondent No.1 and the deceased and that accident had occurred during and in course of the employment and taking the salary of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- p.m. and his age as 22 years applying the factor of 221.37
, held that claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.5,53,425/- and also awarded Rs.15,000/- towards Funeral expenses.
The Commissioner however fixed the liability of payment of compensation on the owner of the vehicle on the premise that the deceased did not possess the valid driving license.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant/claimant is before this Court.

6. Sri. S.S.Mamadapur, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant at the outset submits that even if there was a breach of terms of insurance policy in the nature of the deceased not having valid driving license, the NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 Commissioner ought to have directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and thereafter recover the same.

7. Relying upon the judgment of the Gurmail Singh V. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. and another reported in 2019 ACJ 713, wherein it is held that the Insurance Company be first directed to pay the compensation and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Gurmail Singh V. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. and another reported in 2019 ACJ 713
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that following the said dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court, respondent no.2 - Insurance Company be directed to deposit the amount in the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

8. As regards the assessment of income is concerned he refers to the notification dated 31.05.2010 issued by the Central Government in exercise of the power under Section 4(1)(b) of Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 and hence submits that Commissioner ought to have NC:
Smt. Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16179811/
3 2023:KHC-K:8642 taken into consideration is Rs.8,000/-.

entities.text: Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he submits that on these two counts the appeal be allowed.

9. Per contra, Sri.Sudarshan M, learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company relying upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of BELI RAM VS. RAJINDER KUMAR in Civil Appeal Nos.7220- 7221/2011 submits that since admittedly deceased did not have the valid driving license the respondent No.2/Insurance Company cannot be fasten with the liability of paying the compensation.
He submits that order of the Commissioner exonerating the respondent No.2/Insurance Company cannot be found fault with and hence seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
11.

The Substantial Questions of law that arise for consideration are;
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 "(1) Whether the Commissioner is justified in absolving the respondent/Insurance Company from payment of compensation on the premise of deceased not having valid license?
and (2) Whether the Commissioner is justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-
p.m. in the light of the notification dated 31.05.2010 issued by the Central Government fixing the minimum wages at Rs.8,000/-p.m?
12.

The Apex Court in the case of BELI RAM VS. RAJINDER KUMAR AND OTHERS in Civil Appeal Nos.7220-7221/2011 at para 21 has held as under;
"21.

entities.text: BELI RAM VS. RAJINDER KUMAR AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Judge debated the question of the consequences of the MV Act being a beneficial piece of legislation.

Thus, if two interpretations were possible, it was opined that the one which is in favour of the claimants should be given, but violence should not be done to the clear and plain language of the statute.

Thus, while protecting the rights of the claimants by asking the insurance company to deposit the amount, the recovery of the same from the insured would follow as the sympathy can only be for the victim of the accident.
The right which has to be protected, is of the victim and not the owner of the vehicle.

It was, thus, observed in para 18 as under:
"18.

When an employer employees a driver, it is his duty to check that the driver is duly licensed to drive the vehicle. Section- 5 of the Motor Vehicles Act provides that no owner or person incharge of a motor vehicle shall cause or NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 permit any person to drive the vehicle if he does not fulfil the requirements of Sections 3 and 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The owner must show that he has verified the licence.
He must also take reasonable care to see that his employee gets his licence renewed within time.
In my opinion, it is no defence for the owner to plead that he forgot that the driving licence of his employee had to be renewed.
A person when he hands his motor vehicle to a driver owes some responsibility to society at large.
Lives of innocent people are put to risk in case the vehicle is handed over to a person not duly licensed.

Therefore, there must be some evidence to show that the Smt. Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16179811/
4 owner had either checked the driving licence or had given instructions to his driver to get his driving licence renewed on expiry thereof.

entities.text: Smt. Suguladevi vs Sri. Husainbasha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, no such evidence has been led.
In view of the above discussion, I am clearly of the view that there was a breach of the terms of the policy and the Insurance Company could not have been held liable to satisfy the claim."
13. In the instant case, admittedly the deceased did not possess the driving license.
As such, the order of the Commissioner exonerating the respondent/Insurance Company cannot be found fault with.

14. Notwithstanding the same in the light of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of GURMAIL SINGH V. BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ANOTHER reported in 2019 ACJ 713 and also - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 considering the object of the legislation which is a beneficial legislation and considering the status of the claimant being the widowed mother of the deceased who was completely depending upon his earnings, this Court is of the considered view that respondent No.2/Insurance Company be directed to pay the compensation on the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the respondent No.1.

entities.text: GURMAIL SINGH V. BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ANOTHER reported in 2019 ACJ 713
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, first substantial question of law is answered.

15. By Notification dated 31.05.2010 the Central Government in exercise of its power under sub-Section (1)(b) of Section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 2023 has notified Rs.8,000/-
p.m.

though in the claim petition it is stated that the deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- p.m.,
considering the concept of just compensation and in view of minimum wages having been fixed by the Central Government it is appropriate that minimum wages of Rs.8,000/- p.m. be taken as the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8642 income of the deceased.

Deducting 50% thereof and applying the factor 221.37 + Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, the claimant is held entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.9,00,480/- (Rs.4,000 X221.37+Rs.15,000) in the place of Rs.5,68,425/-
awarded by the Commissioner.
16. For the foregoing reasons, the appellant is entitled for a sum of Rs.9,00,480/-.
The respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall pay aforesaid compensation at the interest of 12% p.a. from the date of accident till realization.
